passages.heading: Day 1 — The Ache Beneath
passages.text:
mentoring shows up as ambition. Under it is a longing. Welcome to day one of *Becoming a Mentor*. Everything this week is built on a single move — noticing what is already happening inside you before trying to change it.

Career questions look strategic. They rarely are. Under mentoring is usually a longing to matter to a specific someone or something.

The one-line you'll carry today: **mentoring shows up as ambition. Under it is a longing.**

Don't try to make this profound. The whole point of a seven-day arc is that small, honest moves — done in a real body on a real Tuesday — outperform any amount of philosophy. Read the practice once, do it once, and let the rest of the day carry it for you.

passages.heading: Day 2 — Svadharma
passages.text:
Better your own mentoring, done badly, than another's done well. Day 2 of *Becoming a Mentor*. Today we build directly on what yesterday opened.

passages.text:
1. For one waking hour, log every device pickup.
2. Beside each, write: cue, duration, aftermath.
3. Look for the pattern that surprises you.

passages.heading: One-Tab Hour
passages.text:
1. Pick one 60-minute block today.
2. One tab. One task. Phone in another room.
3. When distraction rises, note it on paper, return.
4. End: notice quality difference.

passages.heading: 10 Breaths
passages.text:
1. Sit or stand.
2. Count 10 breaths in and out, only.
3. Lose count? Restart. No punishment.
4. Use before every weekly review session for the rest of the week.

passages.heading: Sit With Nothing
passages.text:
1. Sit for 5 minutes with no input. No music. No phone.
2. Watch what the mind does at minute 2 and 4.
3. Do not resolve. Notice.
4. Return to weekly review refreshed.

passages.heading: Sleep Contract
passages.text:
1. Choose a lights-out time you can hold 5 nights in a row.
2. 60 minutes before: no work, no fast content.
3. 30 minutes before: dim lights.
4. Track it. Sleep is training.

passages.heading: Design The Field
passages.text:
1. Clear one surface entirely.
2. Put one object of intent on it (book, note, image).
3. Remove one visible distraction.
4. Work from this field tomorrow morning.

passages.heading: Stop At 90%
passages.text:
1. In your next work block, set a timer for 25 minutes.
2. Stop when it rings, even if you're mid-sentence.
3. Walk for 5 minutes.
4. Return with fuller attention.

passages.heading: 10 Breaths
passages.text:
1. Sit or stand.
2. Count 10 breaths in and out, only.
3. Lose count? Restart. No punishment.
4. Use before every walking session for the rest of the week.

passages.heading: Sit With Nothing
passages.text:
1. Sit for 5 minutes with no input. No music. No phone.
2. Watch what the mind does at minute 2 and 4.
3. Do not resolve. Notice.
4. Return to walking refreshed.

passages.heading: Sleep Contract
passages.text:
1. Choose a lights-out time you can hold 5 nights in a row.
2. 60 minutes before: no work, no fast content.
3. 30 minutes before: dim lights.
4. Track it. Sleep is training.

passages.heading: Design The Field

3. Remove one visible distraction.

passages.heading: Stop At 90%
passages.text:
1. In your next work block, set a timer for 25 minutes.
2. Stop when it rings, even if you're mid-sentence.
3. Walk for 5 minutes.
4. Return with fuller attention.

passages.heading: Name The Decider
passages.text:
1. Bring your deliberate yes question to mind.
2. Rate 1-10: sleep, hunger, emotional charge, time pressure.
3. If any is under 5, the decision waits.
4. Ask: what would a rested me see here that I can't?

passages.heading: Five Doors
passages.text:
1. Write your deliberate yes question at the top of a page.
2. List 5 possible responses, however unlikely.
3. Add a 6th: "do nothing for 30 days."
4. Sit with all six. Notice which two you'd been trapped between.

passages.heading: Pride Test
passages.text:
1. Take your top 2 options.
2. For each: "If this fails completely, I'll still be proud I chose it because ____."
3. If you can complete the sentence, it survives. If not, it's fear-driven.
4. Notice which survives.

passages.heading: Door Type
passages.text:
1. Ask: is this deliberate yes decision reversible in 6 months?
2. If yes: give yourself 24 hours max and move.
3. If no: give yourself at least a week, and rehearse both futures.
4. Match your process to the door.

passages.heading: Shadow-Life Letter
passages.text:
1. Pick your leading option.
2. Write 3 sentences describing your life 5 years from now on the OTHER path.
3. Include both gains and costs. No romance.
4. Notice: is the shadow life livable? Often the leading option loses its glow.

passages.heading: Five Minutes Watching
passages.text:
1. Sit upright. Close eyes.
2. Watch the breath for 5 minutes.
3. When a deliberate yes thought arises, notice the one who noticed.
4. Rest as the noticer, not the thinker.
5. Ask again: what does the deliberate yes question look like from here?

passages.heading: The Ceremony of Choosing
passages.text:
1. Say the choice out loud in one sentence.
2. Name what you are letting go by choosing.
3. Grieve it — one honest minute.
4. Write the first small action you'll take before Friday.

1. Pick one 60-minute block today.
2. One tab. One task. Phone in another room.
3. When distraction rises, note it on paper, return.
4. End: notice quality difference.

passages.heading: 10 Breaths

2. Count 10 breaths in and out, only.
3. Lose count? Restart. No punishment.
4. Use before every complaint fast session for the rest of the week.

passages.heading: Sit With Nothing

2. Watch what the mind does at minute 2 and 4.
3. Do not resolve. Notice.
4. Return to complaint fast refreshed.

passages.heading: Sleep Contract

passages.heading: Design The Field

4. Work from this field tomorrow morning.

3. Walk for 5 minutes.
4. Return with fuller attention.

passages.text:

2. Bring kindness to mind.
3. Feel the physical sensation, not the story.
4. Say inside: "I'm here. You can be here too."

passages.heading: Find The Origin
passages.text:
1. Ask: "When did I first feel exactly this?"
2. Wait. Don't force it.
3. When something arises, write one line about it.
4. Notice the age of kindness.

passages.heading: Offer It Up
passages.text:
1. Sit. Hand on heart.
2. Bring the person or situation of kindness to mind.
3. Whisper: "For your wellbeing, not mine."
4. Repeat 21 times.

passages.heading: One Clean Sentence
passages.text:
1. Identify the kindness situation where a limit is overdue.
2. Write the sentence, no adjectives.
3. Read it aloud to the mirror.
4. Deliver it before Friday.

passages.heading: Release Ritual
passages.text:
1. Sit. Bring the person or self to mind.
2. Say: "I am not agreeing. I am putting this down."
3. Physically open your hands.
4. Breathe out longer than in.

passages.heading: Three Absences
passages.text:
1. Name three things in your life that, if gone tomorrow, you would grieve.
2. Name them out loud.
3. Feel the pull of them, not the concept.
4. Rest there.

passages.heading: Signature Prayer
passages.text:
1. Write a 3-line prayer about kindness.
2. Read it aloud.
3. Say it once each morning for 30 days.
4. Notice what changes in you, not in the situation.

2. Write what they need.
3. Ask: is my week aligned to that need?
4. Adjust one thing tomorrow.

3. Tell one person.

passages.heading: The Refusal

2. Say each aloud.
